column1: # Unreal: nninitStartup reserves a 62 GB address region and its FMallocBinned3 takes 37 GB of it. The rewriter cuts the allocator in any Unreal 4 / 5 main (dm/tools/ue_malloc.py) and gives
# the region what the alias region has room for (dm/tools/ue_region.py, the gate this build takes: rewrite_main.log's `Unreal's engine region: reserved at 0x16344e0 in nninitStartup's
# 0x1633e70, its size stored from x8`). The alias region is the one an iPhone can reserve, and every Unreal 4 / 5 profile here uses the same partition on a phone (OCTOPATH TRAVELER 0,
# DRAGON QUEST VII Reimagined, FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, SMT V: Vengeance, OCTOPATH TRAVELER II): alias 3.125 GB, 3.75 GB in all, 256 MB stacks, heap 0.125 GB. iOS: alias = mem_alias, so
# g_reserve = 3.75 - 3.125 + 3.125 = 3.75 GB, and the engine region gets the alias region less the SDK's 62 MB node area and 256 MB for regions made later, 2.81 GB.
# The Mac's alias region is max(mem_alias, the Switch's 64 GB) (hle_svc.c), so g_reserve = 3.75 - 3.125 + 64 = 64.625 GB (0x1028000000) and the heap region 3.75 - 3.125 - 0.25 - 0.25 = 0.125 GB:
# the layout a 64.62 GB profile gave it, unchanged, because the block it adds back takes nothing from the heap. Address space, not memory: the application pool bounds what is mapped.
# Was mem_reserve 0x1028000000 / mem_alias 0x1000000000 (the Mac's numbers), which on iOS asked for one 64.62 GB reservation, and an iPhone cannot place it: `FATAL reserve guest AS` in
# mem_init_once, the device's largest free block 51.00 GB (log GTAIII ipa, 2026-11-14).
# the NPDM declares 80 MB of system resource
# The shaders are inline in pakchunk0-Switch.pak, in the two forms Unreal keeps without a shader code archive: the cooked packages (map rows pakchunk0-Switch.pak#Engine/Content/…
# .uexp#UE<offset>, 4,399 keys) and the engine's global shader cache (pakchunk0-Switch.pak#Engine/GlobalShaderCache-GLSL_SWITCH.bin, 1,780). No source path names a
# "ShaderArchive-" code archive, so every row lands in the split's "other" group; the key is required and kept as the provisional profile guessed it. 15,651 pak entries do
# not decode (a reader limit on those pak blocks), and 37 keys reached only through run-time captures are not in this map (README.md)

column1: # 60 fps: Unreal's own limit, found by name in main by the rewriter (ue_cvar.py; main.fixups.tsv UE_CVAR:t.MaxFPS 0x7584630, which is
# FPSLocker's t.MaxFPS object for this build 0x7584640 minus its +0x10 value pointer). hle_fpslock.c writes the game thread's and the
# render thread's copies every frame they differ, and rhi.SyncInterval (0x7455a40) 2 -> 1 vsync. The present cap at 60 makes the host
# present one vsync a frame (hle_nvn.c present_itv), so neither the game's present interval 2 nor a display-mode cut is needed.
# 120 is a runtime rung (settings.tsv's `120=120 fps?DM_GAME_FPS_MAX==120`): fps_max only unlocks it, the default stays 60. On the Mac and on iOS, where the cap reads
# front_screen_max_fps: an iPad Pro's ProMotion screen shows it, a 60 Hz screen stays at 60.
# fps_high() (hle_nvn.c) refuses 120 without an engine limiter the host writes; this title HAS one (UE_CVAR:t.MaxFPS in main.fixups.tsv,
# dm_fps_lock_engine true) and has no frame step page (dm_fps_state 0), so the gate passes with this key at 120.
# the engine's limiter sleeps a whole frame period (1/MaxFPS) and subtracts none of the frame's work, so any value near the target lands after the
# host's 60 Hz tick and costs a tick: measured in one run on this build (p50 frame time) t.MaxFPS 60 -> 33.45 ms (30.0 fps), 61 -> 21.0, 120 -> 22.6-25.4,
# 240 -> 17.0, 0 -> 16.48 (60.7 fps). So the host writes 0 (no engine limit) and its present cap at 60 paces the frames; the game steps by the time that
# passed, so 60 is the same speed as 30 (FPSLocker's 60 fps patch for this build does the same: its ALL_FPS entry writes t.MaxFPS and r.VSync only).
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 in the check boot: the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
